title: SC PSC Order No. 2026-157H — Standing Hearing Officer Directive Order Granting Request for Confidential Treatment - Jeremiah Clem, Complainant/Petitioner v. Duke Energy Progress, LLC, Defendant/Respondent
summary: Standing Hearing Officer Directive Order Granting Request for Confidential Treatment - Jeremiah Clem, Complainant/Petitioner v. Duke Energy Progress, LLC, Defendant/Respondent
text:
PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION OF SOUTH CAROLINA 
STANDING HEARING OFFICER DIRECTIVE 
DOCKET NO. 2026-137-E ORDER NO. 2026-157-H 
JULY 7, 2026 
STANDING HEARING OFFICER: C. Jo Anne Wessinger Hill, Esquire 
DOCKET DESCRIPTION: 
DOCKET NO. 2026-137-E – Jeremiah Clem, Complainant/Petitioner v. Duke Energy Progress, 
LLC, Defendant/Respondent 
MATTER UNDER CONSIDERATION: 
Request by Duke Energy Progress, LLC (“DEP” or “Company”) for the Commission to grant 
Confidential Treatment to certain portions of the Company’s Verified Motion for Summary 
Judgment and Answer of Duke Energy Progress, LLC, filed on June 25, 2026 (Request). 
HEARING OFFICER’S ACTION: This matter comes before the Hearing Officer on 
the Request of Duke Energy Progress, LLC (“DEP” or “Company”) seeking Confidential 
Treatment for certain identified and marked portions of the Company’s Verified Motion for 
Summary Judgment and Answer of Duke Energy Progress, LLC, which discuss customer 
specific data and information under S.C. Code Ann. Regs. 103-823.2(3). 
The Request was filed on June 25, 2026, in the cover letter accompanying DEP’s Verified Motion 
for Summary Judgment and Answer, collectively referred hereafter as “Motion and Answer.” DEP 
filed a confidential version of DEP’s Motion and Answer under seal with the Commission, as well 
as submitted the redacted public version of its Motion and Answer. This Request is made pursuant 
to the South Carolina Freedom of Information Act, S.C. Code Ann. §§ 30-4-10, et. seq., S.C. Code 
Ann. Regs. 103-804 and Commission Orders No. 2005-226, 2020-490, 2023-859, and 2025-321. 
In submitting the Request, DEP asserts the need to protect the redacted information from public 
disclosure because DEP needed to discuss this identified specific customer data as part its Motion 
and Answer in defense of the claims asserted by the Petitioner. It also asserts that this identified 
information is specific to the Complainant/Petitioner and is considered personal information which 
should be protected from public disclosure or release. Request, p. 1. DEP also asks for the 
Commission to exclude this identified information from public disclosure under the Freedom of 
Information Act, S.C. Code Ann. §§ 30-4-10, et. seq. 
Commission Regulation 103-804(S)(2) provides that the Commission, within its discretion, can 
determine what matters are placed and available in the public record on the DMS. S.C. Code Ann. 
Regs. 103-804(S)(2) (2012). Likewise, the Commission has discretion to determine what matters 
are exempt from public disclosure, including exemption from release under the Freedom of 
Information Act, S.C. Code Ann. §§ 30-4-10 et seq. 
Considering the Request of Duke Energy Progress, LLC, and its actions in compliance with 
Commission Orders No. 2005-226, 2020-490, 2023-859 and applicable laws, the Hearing Officer 
finds and concludes that confidential treatment and protection from public release is

warranted for the specific identified customer information discussed in the Company’s 
Verified Motion for Summary Judgment and Answer and concerns the account or business 
transaction(s) between Jeremiah Clem, who is the Complainant/Petitioner, and the 
Company in this matter. 
Accordingly, the Request for Confidential Treatment and for Protective Order is granted as 
requested by Duke Energy Progress, LLC, for the information identified as customer specific 
data about the Complainant/Petitioner’s account with Duke Energy Progress, LLC, which 
is discussed in the Verified Motion for Summary Judgment and Answer of Duke Energy 
Progress, LLC. This Standing Hearing Officer Directive shall also serve as the Protective 
Order. 
The Hearing Officer further finds and concludes that the non-redacted confidential version of the 
Verified Motion for Summary Judgment and Answer of Duke Energy Progress, LLC, is exempt 
from disclosure under the Freedom of Information Act, S.C. Code Ann. §§ 30-4-10 et seq. 
Therefore, the request is granted to exempt the identified customer specific information discussed 
in the Motion and Answer submitted by Duke Energy Progress, LLC, from public disclosure 
pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act. 
The Commission shall maintain as confidential and/or exempt from disclosure under the Freedom 
of Information Act the non-redacted confidential version of the Verified Motion for Summary 
Judgment and Answer of Duke Energy Progress, LLC, to protect the Complainant/Petitioner 
Jeremiah Clem unless, or until, the Commission rules such information is not entitled to protection 
from public disclosure, or Complainant/Petitioner Jeremiah Clem and Duke Energy Progress, 
LLC, agree that such information is no longer subject to protection or confidentiality. 
On behalf of the Commission, this Hearing Officer further accepts for filing both the nonredacted 
confidential version and the redacted public version of the Verified Motion for Summary Judgment 
and Answer filed by Duke Energy Progress, LLC, in this Docket. 
The fact that the Motion for Confidential Treatment and Protective Order is granted does not have 
any bearing on any potential findings, conclusions, report, or decision in this matter. Additionally, 
this Standing Hearing Officer Directive does not examine or discuss the merits of the underlying 
Complaint and Answer. It is limited only to the protection and confidentiality of the certain 
customer specific data identified and discussed in the Motion and Answer by Duke Energy 
Progress, LLC. 
This concludes the Hearing Officer’s Directive.
